title: Full English Breakfast
subtitle: The complete British cooked breakfast
excerpt: Back bacon, pork sausages, fried egg, baked beans, grilled tomato, sautéed mushrooms, and black pudding: the full English, cooked so everything is ready at the same time and served with buttered toast.

recipe.sourceNotes: The full English breakfast, also called the fry-up, cooked breakfast, or Full English, evolved from the Victorian country-house tradition of the elaborate breakfast sideboard, where guests helped themselves to multiple hot dishes. By the early twentieth century a simpler version had become a British national institution, eaten across classes in transport cafes, greasy spoons, hotels, and homes. The components vary by region and personal conviction: black pudding is common in the north and Midlands, less so in the south; baked beans are a twentieth-century addition that would have surprised Victorians; fried bread is a regional alternative to toast. The ordering in which the components are cooked matters: sausages need the longest time and go in first; eggs go in last. Everything should be ready simultaneously.

recipeTools.notes: A large frying pan for the bacon, sausages, eggs, and mushrooms.

content.text: Everything must arrive at the table hot and at the same time. Work in sequence: sausages first (longest), then bacon and tomatoes, then mushrooms, then eggs last. Keep completed items warm in a low oven while finishing the eggs. Baked beans are heated in a small saucepan off to one side.

Heat the oven to 100 C. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the sausages and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, turning regularly, until browned all over and cooked through. Transfer to a plate in the oven to keep warm.

In the same pan, fry the bacon over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side. Alongside, cook the tomatoes cut-side down for 2 minutes, then flip and cook for 1 minute more. If using black pudding, fry in the same pan for 2 minutes per side. Transfer everything to the oven.

Add the butter to the pan and cook the mushrooms over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and any liquid has evaporated. Season. Push to the side, add a little more butter, and fry the eggs to your preference: sunny-side up for runny yolks, or flip for over-easy.
Heat the baked beans in a small saucepan. Arrange everything on warmed plates with the toast and serve immediately.
